representative_tasks.task: Is a paraphrased answer faithful to its retrieved source?
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Recognizes a faithful paraphrase and separates faithfulness from correctness

representative_tasks.task: Faithfulness passes but retrieved documents conflict (stale vs current policy)
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Identifies the conflicting-sources failure mode and fixes it at retrieval/ranking/indexing

representative_tasks.task: Score unlabeled eval queries as 0 recall / 0 reciprocal rank to keep the denominator
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Treats unlabeled metrics as undefined, reports the labeled-subset metric with the skipped count

negative_cases: Request to report one blended RAG score instead of separate retrieval and generation metrics (planned)
rubric: Fix placed at the right layer
Unlabeled queries excluded from retrieval means and counted
prerequisites: Executable tests referenced by cases need no third-party packages; numpy and scikit-learn are used only by the nDCG cross-check test
execution_constraints: Offline grading and fixture self-tests need only Python 3.10+ stdlib and no network.
Executable tests need the example-test dependencies (see docs/EXAMPLE-TESTS.md) and run via run_evals.py --run-executable.
Model-mode runs need --provider anthropic --model <id> --allow-network and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; they cost money and are not deterministic.
expected_artifacts: Retrieval metrics that return NaN for unlabeled queries and a printed skipped-query count
known_limitations: Hard assertions are regexes over the response text: they verify that key concepts are stated, not that the reasoning connecting them is correct.
No baseline (with-skill vs without-skill) has been measured for this skill; any uplift claim requires a recorded or model run.
